info.name: Umari OS API
info.description:
Postman collection for Umarí OS API.

This collection is organized by backend module and uses collection variables for credentials, tokens, IDs and reusable data. It must be exported without real credentials, tokens or private establishment data.

Use the Auth folders to initialize tokens before running protected module requests.

request.description:
This is a GET request and it is used to "get" data from an endpoint. There is no request body for a GET request, but you can use query parameters to help specify the resource you want data on (e.g., in this request, we have `id=1`).

A successful GET response will have a `200 OK` status, and should include some kind of response body - for example, HTML web content or JSON data.
Authenticates a admin user. Stores `admin_token`, `admin_refresh_token`, `admin_session_id`, plus current `auth_token` and `auth_refresh_token` variables.
Authenticates a kds user. Stores `kds_token`, `kds_refresh_token`, `kds_session_id`, plus current `auth_token` and `auth_refresh_token` variables.
Authenticates a cashier user. Stores `cashier_token`, `cashier_refresh_token`, `cashier_session_id`, plus current `auth_token` and `auth_refresh_token` variables.
Authenticates a waiter user. Stores `waiter_token`, `waiter_refresh_token`, `waiter_session_id`, plus current `auth_token` and `auth_refresh_token` variables.
Authenticates a user user. Stores `user_token`, `user_refresh_token`, `user_session_id`, plus current `auth_token` and `auth_refresh_token` variables.
Returns the authenticated user using `auth_token`. If the access token is tied to a revoked session, this must return 401.

item.name: Auth - Audit Events
item.description:
Folder de validación manual para AAT-11. Estos requests no consultan directamente la tabla `auditoria`; disparan eventos de autenticación que deben verificarse en base de datos con la consulta documentada en el README.

Eventos esperados:
- `AUTH_LOGIN_SUCCESS`
- `AUTH_LOGIN_FAILED`
- `AUTH_REFRESH_SUCCESS`
- `AUTH_REFRESH_FAILED`
- `AUTH_LOGOUT`

Consulta recomendada:

```sql
select
  id_auditoria,
  id_usuario,
  id_establecimiento,
  tabla_afectada,
  registro_id,
  accion,
  datos_nuevos,
  ip_origen,
  user_agent,
  created_at
from auditoria
where accion like 'AUTH_%'
order by created_at desc
limit 30;
```

La auditoría no debe guardar contraseñas, access tokens, refresh tokens ni hashes de refresh token.

request.description: Dispara un login correcto para validar el registro `AUTH_LOGIN_SUCCESS` en `auditoria`. La respuesta actualiza `auth_token`, `auth_refresh_token` y `auth_session_id` para continuar el flujo de auditoría.

exec: pm.test("Response contains tokens and session", function () {

request.description: Dispara un login fallido para validar el registro `AUTH_LOGIN_FAILED` en `auditoria`. También puede retornar `429` si el rate limit ya fue alcanzado durante pruebas repetidas.

exec: pm.test("Login failed returns 401 or rate limit 429", function () {

request.description: Renueva la sesión actual y dispara `AUTH_REFRESH_SUCCESS`. La prueba actualiza `auth_token` y `auth_refresh_token` porque el backend rota refresh tokens.

exec: pm.test("Response contains rotated tokens and session", function () {

request.description: Dispara un refresh inválido para validar `AUTH_REFRESH_FAILED` en `auditoria`. No debe registrar el refresh token enviado.
Cierra la sesión actual y dispara `AUTH_LOGOUT`. Ejecutar después de login/refresh porque revoca la sesión representada por `auth_token`.
